prompt:
Image 1 is the pose guide: a grey clay maquette of this standing stone in one action, rendered from the game's battle camera. Copy from it exactly the camera angle, the direction the body faces, the pose, and the figure's size and place in the frame. Do not copy its smooth clay surfaces, its simplified round shapes or the thickness of its limbs: the body, its anatomy and every detail follow Image 2.
Image 2 is the approved painted game cutout of this exact standing stone, standing at rest, seen from the same camera in the same view. Paint the same individual, with exactly the same head, shapes, proportions, colours, materials, markings and equipment, in the same painting style and the same light, now in the action of Image 1.

One large painted standing stone, full body, alone in the image on a perfectly flat, uniform pure green (#00FF00) background, as a game cutout. Action: shattered: the standing stone broken across a third of the way up; the stump still stands on its mound of earth and roots, and the upper part lies broken in three heavy chunks on the mound, the glyphs still on them, with small stones and dust around.

Camera: high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at a miniature on a table; orthographic, with no perspective. The standing stone faces away from us, toward the upper right of the image, as in Image 1 and Image 2: we see its back, its right side and the top of its head from behind; its face is hidden. It is foreshortened as seen from above: the top of the head, the shoulders or back and the upper body are large, the legs short.

Light: outdoor daylight, exactly as in Image 2; the figure stays as dark and as muted as in Image 2, lit only by small warm and cool highlights, never washed out or brightened. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top and the upper-left side with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows. Nothing glows more than it does in Image 2. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, exactly the hand of Image 2; a muted earthy palette with its own colours exactly as Image 2 shows them; soft painterly edges, small crisp highlights and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. A strong, simple, readable silhouette in every pose. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The god: the Living Monolith, a god that is a single great standing stone: immobile, ancient and aware. Colours: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the stone is the pigment in its carved glyphs: dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Nothing in the image glows: the glyphs are pigment in carved grooves. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.
Body: one tall, rough-hewn slab of grey granite (#7D7A75), about three times as tall as it is wide and a third as thick, its edges weathered and chipped, no capstone: its top is a plain, flat, broken edge; no moss, no vines, no overgrowth; no face, no eyes, no carved features. Glyphs: rows of deeply carved runic glyphs running down both of its broad faces, the grooves filled with a pigment of dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Base: its foot is rooted in the ground: it rises from a low mound of dark earth and stones, with thick old roots gripping its base.
The same rows of carved glyphs run down both of its broad faces, the front and the back, so that the colour shows from either side.

Size: the figure fills the image exactly as its maquette does in Image 1, in the same place, with at least 24 pixels of clean background all round; nothing is cropped.

Background: one flat pure green (#00FF00) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow. No green anywhere on the figure: no green cloth, no green glow, no green reflections.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, dividing lines between the cells, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; other creatures or people; a cropped figure; fire, flames, breath, smoke, sparks, floating embers, magic light or mist (the game draws every effect).
